pr_title: Fully disable vim mode on start unless it's enabled
pr_body:
Fixes #685 

* Completely ignore `VimState::mode` when we're disabled.
* I made some structural adjustments to remove the need for defer. Instead of accessing the global in associated VimState functions, we now have a single `VimState::update_global` method that allows us to call its mutable instance methods.
* I adjusted `observe_global` to take a reference to the global being observed.

/cc @Kethku
pr_comments: I'm bothered that the test which handles enabling and disabling vim mode didn't catch the issues in my branch before merging. Should we add a test which catches the issue as it existed before these fixes?

I can't address this right now, but I'll take a closer look tonight. I think the remaining problem in this branch is just switching to normal mode when re-enabling. I should have commented on my PR that this needed some more manual testing.

I noticed the settings issues last night and did a partial fix but left it without comment for later. I'll try to remember to capture any outstanding problems or need for manual testing with PRs in a comment in the future
@Kethku I force-pushed a new sequence of commits with a test that fails to demonstrate the original problem.

I'm going to merge this so we can get a working version of 0.23 considering I jumped the gun on merging #682. Happy to discuss stuff in here and make changes going forward, but I think it represents an improvement over the current state so let's just roll with it.

issue_context.title: Seeing a block cursor and unable to type when `vim_mode` is `false`
issue_context.body:
After building a candidate v0.23.0 tag, it seems Vim mode isn't being fully disabled even if I have `vim_mode: false` in my settings. I see a block cursor and can't type, but I also can't get into insert mode and can move the cursor with the non-Vim bindings.

/cc @Kethku
comments: Thats very frustrating. I'll look into it shortly. I thought I had fixed this, but probably broke it in my last fix

review_comments: setting the mode to normal when re-enabled will fix the test and I think is a small polish issue to make things more predictable.
Removing here feels like a footgun. Although you do have a reference to the global, if you call functions which depend on the global from a global notification, you'd find that its gone.
So are you saying you think it would be preferable to let the user read it out if they need it? It just seems a bit annoying to not get a reference to the thing you're observing.
